acceptance.given: A repair run is executed against a repository with a recorded historical tracked-membership snapshot.

oracle.expected: The before/after comparison reports identical historical tracked membership and the repair evidence is append-only.
forbidden: Any added, removed, or altered historical tracked membership
oracle.observable: The S6 membership comparison assertion in scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s6.py passes and reports an unchanged tracked-membership set.

acceptance.then: The repair completes without modifying historical tracked membership.

failure_intents.selector_intent: py -3 -m pytest scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s6.py must fail if the before/after tracked-membership comparison detects any addition, removal, or alteration.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve historical tracked membership exactly while allowing append-only repair evidence; the test compares membership before and after repair.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; rollback restores only the Toolchain implementation while retaining historical membership.

slice_hint.state_transition: historical tracked membership exists -> repair executes -> historical tracked membership remains identical
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S6 test passes with an exact before/after membership match and no mutation reported.

acceptance.given: Pinned evaluation inputs and their expected semantic verdict are available for a clean checkout.

oracle.expected: Evaluation in a fresh checkout produces the same semantic verdict and coverage result as the pinned-input evaluation.
forbidden: A semantic verdict or coverage result differing from the pinned-input evaluation
oracle.observable: The S24 replay test records equal pinned-input and fresh-checkout verdict and coverage outputs.

acceptance.then: The fresh-checkout result is accepted as reproducible only when verdict and coverage both match.
acceptance.when: When pinned inputs are evaluated in a fresh checkout.

failure_intents.selector_intent: py -3 -m pytest scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s24.py must fail when fresh-checkout replay produces a verdict or coverage result different from pinned inputs.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Replay pinned inputs from a fresh checkout and compare both semantic verdict and coverage result to the pinned baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema migration; replay behavior remains compatible with existing seed manifests.

slice_hint.state_transition: pinned inputs evaluated -> fresh checkout recreated -> verdict and coverage compared -> reproducibility accepted or rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 test passes only when fresh-checkout verdict and coverage exactly equal the pinned evaluation.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has succeeded and includes its command execution metadata.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result records an independent verification of the command identity and execution facts before acceptance.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result lacking independent command verification
oracle.observable: The S24 replay assertion confirms command verification is performed independently and persisted in the result evidence.

acceptance.then: The Replay Result is accepted only after independent command verification succeeds.

failure_intents.selector_intent: py -3 -m pytest scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s24.py must fail when a successful Replay Result omits or falsifies independent command verification.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each successful replay result to independently verify its command and record that verification in the result evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing replay result consumers remain compatible; only missing verification causes rejection.

slice_hint.state_transition: replay succeeds -> command independently verified -> verification recorded -> result accepted
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 assertion passes only when independent command verification is present and correct in the successful result.

acceptance.given: The repair starts with a recorded native command identity for the Toolchain replay path.

oracle.expected: Before/after comparison shows the native command identity is unchanged by repair.
forbidden: Replacing or changing the identity of the native command
oracle.observable: The replay identity assertion compares the recorded command identity before and after repair and reports equality.

acceptance.then: Repair is accepted only if the native command identity remains byte-for-byte and semantically unchanged.

failure_intents.selector_intent: py -3 -m pytest scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s24.py must fail when the before/after native command identity differs.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve the native replay command identity across repair and explicitly compare it before and after the change.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; rollback restores command construction without changing its established identity.

slice_hint.state_transition: native command identity exists -> repair executes -> identity compared -> unchanged identity accepted
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 identity assertion passes only when the native command identity before and after repair is identical.
